title: Private Delivery and Day-2 Operational Contracts for Private Deployments
author: Arielle Chen
content:
Overview:

This document defines the delivery (pre-install and install) checklist, the operational contracts (SLOs, monitoring, alerting, maintenance windows), Day-2 expectations (observability, capacity, support procedures), and the canonical upgrade / rollback procedure for Redwood private deployments (VPC and on-prem bundles). It is intended for Redwood delivery engineers, customer SREs, and customer platform teams.

Scope and audience:
- Scope: Private (VPC and on-prem) deployments of Redwood Inference control plane and runtime. Covers delivery gates, packaging expectations, telemetry and alerting contracts, upgrade/rollback flow, and customer responsibilities.
- Audience: Delivery engineers, Customer SREs, Redwood Solutions Engineering, and Support.

Goals and non-goals:
- Goals:
  - Establish objective, testable delivery gates before handoff to customer operations.
  - Specify Day-2 observability and alerting that Redwood will provide vs. customer required telemetry sinks.
  - Describe a deterministic, reversible upgrade path with clear rollback triggers.
- Non-goals:
  - Host-specific cloud provider IaC (see reference-architectures).
  - Deep model onboarding steps after platform is operational.

Summary of operational contracts (high level):
- Availability SLOs (applies to control plane components we operate):
  - control-plane-api: 99.9% monthly uptime for API control-plane endpoints (management, rollout APIs).
  - runtime-proxy (customer-facing router): 99.5% monthly uptime when deployed in Redwood-managed mode.
- Latency SLOs (example targets customers can expect under normal capacity):
  - p95 latency for small completion requests (<=512 tokens): <150ms on dedicated GPU capacity across supported instance families.
  - model-inference p95: dependent on model family; see model profile table during onboarding.
- Error budget and escalation:
  - Error budget: 43.2 minutes/month downtime allowance at 99.9% SLO. Exceeding error budget triggers a severity-2 engagement and a three-week action plan.
  - Escalation: Refer to oncall-and-incident-response/incident-process for chain of command.

Pre-install delivery checklist (gates before scheduled install):
1) Customer prerequisites (must be validated):
   - Hardware inventory: list of target hosts (CPU, RAM, GPU model and count), validated against minimum supported families (NVIDIA A10/A100/H100 equivalents); attach inventory CSV.
   - Network: CIDR blocks, required firewall egress/ingress, and NAT requirements. Required ports:
     - 22/SSH (bastion only), 8443 (control plane API), 50051 (gRPC runtime RPC), 8125 (statsd optional), 9200 (if local ES for logs).
   - DNS: CNAME records for control-plane and runtime endpoints must be provisioned in advance.
   - TLS: Customer-managed certificates preferred; otherwise Redwood can provide cert issuance guidance.
   - KMS & secrets: KMS key ARN or HSM reachability must be available. Key rotation window should be communicated.
   - Time sync: NTP reachable; skew must be <5s across cluster.
2) Packaging and image delivery (customer acceptance):
   - Deployment mode: Identified (VPC-managed, hybrid-control-plane, fully on-prem).
   - Delivery artifact type: OCI registry pull or airgap bundle. For airgap, provide signed tarball + checksums + installation manifest.
   - Signing: All images and bundles must be signed with Redwood release key; customer may provide additional verification steps.
   - Image compatibility matrix attached (OS kernel, container runtime versions).
3) Security & access
   - RBAC mapping: initial admin and read-only roles for customer SREs established.
   - Audit logging: paths and retention policy confirmed.
   - Bastion: Admin access must flow through a hardened bastion; direct SSH onto runtime hosts is discouraged.

On-prem packaging expectations (airgap & thin-installed):
- Ship artifacts as either:
  - OCI repository + Helm charts (preferred for VPC/hybrid installs), or
  - Signed airgap bundle (tar.gz) containing: images.tar, manifests.yaml, installers scripts, SHA256SUMS, signatures, and a verification script.
- Bundle must include a minimal installer that performs preflight checks (disk, ports, kernel modules), verifies signatures, and creates a recovery manifest.
- Versioning: Semantic version tags and a release channel label (stable | canary | rc).
- Unsupported combinations: older kernel <5.10, containerd <1.5 without patching.

Day-2 observability contract (what Redwood provides vs what customer must expose):
- Redwood-provided (out-of-box):
  - Metrics: control_plane_api.requests_total, control_plane_api.latency_ms.p95, runtime.inference.tokens_per_second, kvcache.hit_ratio, gpu.utilization.percent.
  - Logging: structured JSON logs for control-plane and runtime; stdout/stderr aggregated.
  - Traces: OpenTelemetry spans for request lifecycle (ingest -> dispatch -> model runtime).
  - Dashboards: Per-service p50/p95 latency, request rates, error rates, resource utilization.
  - Alerts (default thresholds):
    - control_plane_api.error_rate > 2% sustained for 5m -> paged SRE.
    - runtime.inference.p95 > 2x baseline for 10m -> on-call.
    - gpu.utilization < 10% for 30m while queues backlogged -> investigation.
- Customer responsibilities:
  - Provide ingestion endpoint for covered telemetry (Prometheus remote_write or pushgateway, or a dedicated pull endpoint).
  - Ensure log retention policy and access controls for audit requirements.
  - Provide escalation contacts and local runbooks for physical access.

Standard runbooks (excerpt):
- High-level: service degraded (control plane API 5xx spike)
  1. Verify alert on Redwood dashboard and link to recent deploys.
  2. Check control-plane-api logs: grep for rate-limited errors and downstream DB errors.
  3. If downstream datastore (etcd/Postgres) health is degraded, run health-check scripts and consider failover per datastore guide.
  4. If related to rollout: rollback last canary or scale replicas to baseline.
  5. Post-incident: Run regression tests and update regression-triage with root cause.

Upgrade and rollback process (canonical):
- Principles:
  - All upgrades are staged (canary -> partial -> global).
  - No breaking DB migrations without migration locks and a reversible path.
  - Every upgrade must have a documented verification checklist and automated smoke tests.
- Pre-upgrade gating (must pass):
  - Backup: full config and metadata snapshot stored off-host (S3 or customer-equivalent).
  - Health: all services Healthy for 60m (no critical alerts).
  - Capacity: sufficient spare capacity (recommended +25% headroom).
- Canary upgrade procedure (example):
  1. Create release tag and upload artifacts to target registry/bundle location.
  2. Deploy control-plane components in canary namespace (1 replica or 5% traffic).
  3. Run automated smoke tests (API auth, model list, simple completion request, embeddings endpoint).
  4. Monitor key metrics for 30m: control_plane_api.errors, runtime.inference.p95, gpu.utilization.
  5. If metrics within thresholds, proceed to partial rollout (zone-by-zone).
- Rollback triggers (any of):
  - sustained error rate > 4% for 10m on canary or partial rollout.
  - p95 latency > 3x baseline for 15m and not explained by load spike.
  - failed critical smoke test (auth, model-load, KV cache corruption).
- Rollback steps (fast path):
  1. Stop rollout.
  2. Deploy previous stable tag to affected subset.
  3. Reconcile persistent state if a migration ran (follow migration rollback procedures).
  4. Verify smoke tests and metrics; if green, resume normal operations.

Acceptance tests and gating (minimal list to mark deployment green):
- Smoke tests (must pass):
  - /healthz returns 200 and component statuses are OK.
  - Authentication flows succeed for service accounts.
  - Basic completion request returns expected status and schema.
  - KV cache warms and returns consistent results.
- E2E tests (recommended):
  - Multi-request session preserving KV cache across requests.
  - High-throughput synthetic load to validate autoscaling policies.
  - Latency-sensitive path with small sequence lengths for p95 measurement.

Customer vs Redwood responsibilities (short table):
- Customer provides: physical hardware, network ACLs and ingress/exgress restrictions, DNS and TLS assets, local KMS/HSM access policy enforcement, physical access runbooks.
- Redwood provides: airgap/OCI artifacts, install manifests and verification tooling, baseline dashboards and alerts, upgrade/rollback tooling and runbooks, 30/90/365-day support windows per contract.

Operational SLAs for upgrade windows and maintenance:
- Maintenance windows: standard weekly maintenance window is Sunday 02:00–05:00 local cluster time.
- Notifying changes: Redwood will give 72h notice for non-emergency upgrades; emergency security patches may be applied with 4h notice and full postmortem.

Appendices:
- Example verification commands:
  - kubectl -n redwood get pods --selector app=control-plane -o wide
  - curl -sS -k https://control-plane.example.com/healthz | jq
  - ./installer verify-bundle --bundle ./release-2026-02.tar.gz --sha256 $(cat SHA256SUMS)
- Example smoke test (pseudo-YAML for CI):
  - name: "basic-completion-test"
    run: |
      python tests/smoke_completion.py --endpoint https://runtime.example.com --model small:model-v1 --prompt "Hello"
